intro: To see word count in Pages on Mac, open your document, click View in the toolbar, and choose Show Word Count. A small counter then appears near the bottom of the page, and clicking its arrows lets you switch it to Words.
tldr: Open the document, click View in the toolbar, then choose Show Word Count.
Click the arrows on the counter and pick Words. Characters, paragraphs, and pages are on the same list.
Select text first to count only that part. With no selection, Pages counts the whole document.
Hide the counter with View > Hide Word Count. Page count is separate, under Insert > Page Count.

blocks.text: Word count in Pages is easy to miss because it lives under View, not under Insert or Format where people often look first. Apple's Mac guide covers this feature for Pages 15.4. The same View menu item also shows up in community reports from older releases, including Pages 8.2.1 on macOS 10.15.
Show word count in Pages on Mac

Start by opening the document you want to check. Click View in the toolbar at the top of the window, then choose Show Word Count. A floating counter appears near the bottom of the page. You can keep typing while it stays on screen.

No View button in the toolbar? Use the menu bar instead. Click View at the top of the screen, then choose the same item. OS X Daily's 2022 walkthrough uses this path and says it works in basically every version of Pages for Mac. iGeeksBlog describes a View Options button at the top left, a rectangle icon with a margin. Both paths lead to the same menu, so follow whichever matches your window.
Switch the counter to words, characters, or pages

The counter is not stuck on one number. Click the arrows on its right side to cycle through the options. Apple's guide lists characters with spaces, characters without spaces, words, paragraphs, and pages. You can also click the counter and pick from the same list.

Choose Words for most writing jobs. Word limits on essays, reports, and applications are usually counted in words. Characters matter when a form caps letters or a platform caps posts. Paragraphs help when an editor asks for a set number of them. Check the rules you were given before you trust any number.
Pages remembers your pick. A community user on Pages 8.2.1 reports that the Words choice stuck for new and existing documents. Test it on your own file once, so you know it sticks on your Mac.
Count a selection instead of the whole document

Selection counting saves the most time. Highlight one paragraph and the counter reports only that paragraph. Clear the selection and it returns to the whole document. Apple's guide says the count updates to reflect only the selected text.

Here is a worked example. Say a report has a word limit on one section, and the rest of the report is free. Select only that section. Read the counter. Trim a sentence, then read it again. Each check is quick, and nothing in the file changes while you select.
Hide the counter or move it out of the way

Drag the counter by its body to move it. Apple's guide says it can go anywhere on the window. Put it where it does not cover the lines you are editing. To remove it, choose View > Hide Word Count. The menu item then reads Show Word Count again.

Some Apple Community users say Shift Command W toggles the counter. Apple's guide and OS X Daily do not list that shortcut, so treat it as unofficial. If it does nothing on your Mac, use the View menu. That path is the one Apple documents.
Page count is a different number

Searches for word count often turn up page count, and the two are separate in Pages. To add page count, click where you want the number to appear, then choose Insert > Page Count. Apple's guide says that with unlinked sections, the count covers only the current section and any sections that continue its numbering.

blocks.text: Pages versions and what they need

Pages now comes in two lines on the Mac. MacRumors reports that Pages 15.1 arrived on January 28, 2026, as a separate Apple Creator Studio edition. The older app was updated to 14.5 only to say it will not receive new features of any kind. TidBITS adds that the new app sits beside 14.5 in the Applications folder, under the name Pages Creator Studio.

The version you can run depends on your macOS version. Pages 15.1 needs macOS 15.6 Sequoia or later. Pages 14.5 supports macOS 14.0 Sonoma and later. If your Mac runs an earlier 15.x release, 14.5 is the version you can use. Files move both ways, since TidBITS reports that files made in 15.1 open in 14.x and the reverse.

Creator Studio is a subscription, and you do not need it to count words. Apple lists $12.99 per month or $129 per year for new subscribers. Apple also says Keynote, Pages, Numbers, and Freeform remain free for everyone. The subscription adds premium templates, royalty-free media, and intelligence features.
Pages for iCloud and older Macs

Apple's Pages for iCloud help describes the same flow. You open View, choose Show Word Count, and get a pop-up near the bottom of the page. An arrow on the right shows all statistics, and a selection limits the count to that text. This guide did not test icloud.com, so check the web app once before you rely on it.

Older Macs can show a Page Count label where you expect Word Count. A 2020 Apple Community thread from a Catalina user reports exactly that. The top reply says to click the right edge of the palette and change Page count to Word count, and Pages remembers the change. The original poster did not confirm the fix.
Common mistakes that make the count look wrong

The most common mistake is a leftover selection. If any text is highlighted, the counter reports only that text. A small number then looks like a bug. Click an empty spot in the page to clear the selection, and the full count returns.
The second mistake is reading characters as words. The counter may start on characters because it keeps your last choice. Click the arrows and pick Words before you copy the number anywhere.

The third mistake is mixing up page count and word count. A low page count tells you nothing about the words on those pages. Read the label before you paste the number into an application form or a grading rubric.
Troubleshoot a blank or stuck counter

Some problems come from the app itself, not from your settings. An Apple Community user on Pages 14.4 with macOS Sequoia 15.6 reports empty number boxes in the counter until they click it and choose Words. Turning the count off and on with Shift Command W did not fix it for that user, and the thread has no confirmed fix. If none of the fixes below works, that thread is the place to watch for a confirmed answer.
What to do next with your word count

A visible counter helps most when you already have a target. Writers working to a limit often select each section as they finish it. Students can check a draft against the assignment brief before they submit. If most of your work is drafting, [dictation for writers](/for/writers) covers writing by voice, and [dictation in Pages](/how-to/use-dictation-in-pages) shows the Pages side of it.

Page numbers belong to the document layout, so they are a separate job. If you need them, follow [how to add page numbers in Pages](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-pages). The counter is only a view setting, and you can turn it on or off at any time from the View menu.

faq.question: Where is word count in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: Open the document, click View in the toolbar, then choose Show Word Count. A counter appears near the bottom of the page. If the toolbar is hidden, use View in the menu bar at the top of the screen.

faq.question: How do I see the word count for only part of a document?
faq.answer: Select the text first. The counter then reports only the selected words. Click an empty spot in the page to clear the selection and return to the whole document.

faq.question: Why does my counter show characters instead of words?
faq.answer: The counter keeps the last statistic you used, so it may start on characters. Click its arrows on the right side, or click the counter, and choose Words. A community report for Pages 8.2.1 says that choice persists.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to show word count in Pages?
faq.answer: Some Apple Community users report Shift Command W. Apple's Mac guide does not list it, and OS X Daily does not mention a shortcut. Use View > Show Word Count if the shortcut does nothing.

faq.question: Do I need Apple Creator Studio to see word count in Pages?
faq.answer: No. Apple says Pages stays free for everyone. Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year for new subscribers, and TidBITS reports that creating, viewing, and editing do not require a subscription.

faq.question: Does Pages for iCloud show word count the same way?
faq.answer: Apple's Pages for iCloud help describes the same View menu flow, with a pop-up near the bottom of the page. This guide did not test icloud.com, so confirm it in the web app before you rely on it.

faq.question: Is page count the same as word count in Pages?
faq.answer: No. Word count is under View and counts words, characters, paragraphs, or pages in the counter. Page count is a separate feature, and you add it with Insert > Page Count.

faq.question: Why does my counter show empty number boxes?
faq.answer: An Apple Community user on Pages 14.4 with macOS Sequoia 15.6 reports this. The thread describes clicking the counter and choosing Words as the workaround, but it has no confirmed fix.

steps.name: Open the document
steps.text: Open the Pages document you want to count. Double-click it in Finder, or open Pages and choose File > Open. Apple's Mac guide covers this flow for Pages 15.4, and the steps below follow it.

steps.name: Click View
steps.text: Click View in the toolbar at the top of the Pages window. Apple's guide uses this wording. If you do not see the button, open the View menu in the menu bar at the top of the screen instead.
steps.tip: Some guides call this button View Options. iGeeksBlog describes it as a rectangle icon with a margin at the top left.

steps.name: Choose Show Word Count
steps.text: Choose Show Word Count from the View menu. A counter appears near the bottom of the page. The menu item takes its label from the last statistic you used, so it may read Hide Character Count while the counter is on.

steps.name: Read the counter
steps.text: Look at the number in the counter. If it shows characters or pages instead of words, switch it in the next step. The counter keeps the last statistic you used, so it can start on a number you did not expect.
steps.tip: Community reports for Pages 8.2.1 describe the counter starting on characters by default.

steps.name: Switch the counter to Words
steps.text: Click the arrows on the right side of the counter until the label reads Words. You can also click the counter itself and choose Words from the list. The list also holds characters with and without spaces, paragraphs, and pages.
steps.tip: Test the choice on your own file once to confirm it sticks on your Mac.

steps.name: Select text to count only that part
steps.text: Select a paragraph, a section, or a whole chapter with your mouse or trackpad. The counter updates to show only the selected text. Press ⌘A to select the whole document, and the count covers everything.
steps.tip: Selection counting is the fastest way to check one section against a limit.

steps.name: Clear the selection
steps.text: Click an empty spot in the page to clear the selection. With no selection, the counter goes back to counting the whole document. Check for a selection first if the number looks too small.
steps.tip: A selection you forgot about is the most common cause of a low count.

steps.name: Drag the counter out of the way
steps.text: Drag the counter by its body to any spot on the window. Apple's guide says you can place it anywhere. Keep it off the lines you are editing so it does not cover your text.
steps.tip: Dragging only moves the counter. It does not change the document.

steps.name: Hide the counter
steps.text: Choose View > Hide Word Count when you no longer need the counter. It closes, and the View menu item reads Show Word Count again. Open it again from the same menu at any time.
steps.tip: Shift Command W appears only in Apple Community reports. Apple's guide does not list it, so use the menu if it does nothing.

steps.name: Use Insert > Page Count for pages
steps.text: Page count is a separate feature. Click where you want the number to appear, then choose Insert > Page Count. Apple's guide says that with unlinked sections, the count covers only the current section and sections that continue its numbering.
steps.tip: Page count is not word count. Read the label before you copy the number anywhere.

troubleshooting.fix: Click the counter and choose Words. An Apple Community user on Pages 14.4 with macOS Sequoia 15.6 reports this workaround. Turning the count off and on with Shift Command W did not help that user, and the thread has no confirmed fix.
Click the arrows on the right side of the counter and choose Words. A Pages 8.2.1 user on macOS 10.15 in Apple Community reports that Pages keeps the choice for new and existing documents.

troubleshooting.problem: Menu reads Show Page Count instead of Show Word Count
troubleshooting.fix: This is reported for Pages 8.2.1 on Catalina. Click the right edge of the counter palette and change Page count to Word count. The original poster did not confirm this fix, so check the count against a known section.

troubleshooting.problem: The count is much lower than expected
troubleshooting.fix: A selection is active. Click an empty spot to clear it, then press ⌘A to check the whole document.

troubleshooting.problem: The counter is missing from the window
troubleshooting.fix: If the View menu item says Hide Word Count, the counter is already on, so look for it and drag it into view. If it says Show Word Count, choose it again, then drag the counter to a spot you can see.
That shortcut is unofficial. Apple's Mac guide and OS X Daily do not list it. Use View > Show Word Count instead.
